about: Cloud machines for gpuwm gui. A provider is a table of command lines, run with the user's own CLI and credentials; adding a provider is adding an entry here. {{name}} is filled from the machine row.

aws.label: Amazon EC2
aws.credentials: your own AWS profile (aws configure, or aws sso login), named by the row's profile
aws.user_data:
#!/bin/bash
# First boot: install the ArWen cap guard, which stops this machine at its spend cap or when idle.
mkdir -p /var/lib/arwen-cap-guard
echo {{cap_minutes}} > /var/lib/arwen-cap-guard/cap_minutes
echo {{idle_stop_min}} > /var/lib/arwen-cap-guard/idle_minutes
echo 0 > /var/lib/arwen-cap-guard/used_minutes
cat > /usr/local/bin/arwen-cap-guard <<'GUARD'
#!/bin/bash
# ArWen cap guard: stops this machine at its spend cap or after it sits idle.
# used_minutes is kept on disk, so the cap holds across stops and starts.
state="${ARWEN_CAP_GUARD_STATE:-/var/lib/arwen-cap-guard}"
tick="${ARWEN_CAP_GUARD_TICK_S:-60}"
rounds="${ARWEN_CAP_GUARD_ROUNDS:-0}"
mkdir -p "$state"
count() { cat "$state/$1" 2>/dev/null || echo "$2"; }
# A boot is billed before this service runs: count one minute for it.
echo $(( $(count used_minutes 0) + 1 )) > "$state/used_minutes"
idle=0; n=0
while sleep "$tick"; do
  used=$(( $(count used_minutes 0) + 1 ))
  echo "$used" > "$state/used_minutes"
  cap=$(count cap_minutes 0)
  limit=$(count idle_minutes 30)
  if [ "$used" -ge "$cap" ]; then shutdown -h now 'spend cap reached'; fi
  # A render worker waiting for frames is not work: only its drawing (python -m gpuwm render) is.
  if pgrep -af 'python[0-9.]* .*-m gpuwm|machine_agent' | grep -v ' render-loop ' |
       awk -v me="$$" '$1 != me' | grep -q . \
     || nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid --format=csv,noheader 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
    idle=0
  else
    idle=$((idle + 1))
  fi
  echo "$idle" > "$state/idle_count"
  if [ "$idle" -ge "$limit" ]; then shutdown -h now 'idle stop'; fi
  n=$((n + 1))
  if [ "$rounds" -gt 0 ] && [ "$n" -ge "$rounds" ]; then exit 0; fi
done
GUARD
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/arwen-cap-guard
cat > /etc/systemd/system/arwen-cap-guard.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=ArWen spend cap and idle stop
[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/arwen-cap-guard
Restart=always
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now arwen-cap-guard.service
